notes.text: Allow a global maximum number of concurrently running development servers, for example two counting-semaphore slots.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Implemented the persisted optional counting semaphore across the shared ControlService used by HTTP and MCP. The dashboard can enable a limit from 1 to 64 and shows usage and holders; service status and the MCP get_server_capacity tool expose the same state. Starts acquire atomically, switches retain their slot, failures release it, and lowering the limit preserves running servers. Focused tests cover contention for the final slot, capacity exhaustion, switch retention, failed-start release, persistence, HTTP, MCP, and localization. Keep the item open until the rebuilt controller is explicitly installed and exercised with real managed processes; the active service was not restarted implicitly.

problem: Several independent projects can currently start at once without a global resource budget. On a development host, agents or humans can therefore consume enough memory and CPU to disrupt the primary development workload.

risk.rollback: Disable the capacity gate while retaining the configured value and audit history. Never stop already running servers merely because the configured limit is lowered.

scope: Add a controller-wide configurable capacity expressed as a counting semaphore; each starting or running managed server consumes one slot regardless of development or production mode.

Acquire a slot atomically before starting a stopped project and release it after a failed start or confirmed stop. Switching a running project retains its existing slot and must not transiently require a second one.
Return an explicit capacity-exhausted result instead of silently queueing; show the configured limit, used slots, and projects holding them in the dashboard, CLI, status API, and MCP read tools.
Keep project reservations separate from capacity: a human lock or agent lease protects ownership but consumes a capacity slot only while its server is starting or running.
When the limit is reduced below current usage, keep current servers alive and refuse new starts until usage falls within the new limit.
title: Limit concurrently running managed servers
validation: With capacity two, start two projects concurrently and verify a third start or stopped-project claim is rejected without spawning a process.
Verify two simultaneous requests for the last slot cannot both start, including requests arriving through HTTP and MCP.
Verify switching an already running project retains its slot and a failed start releases its slot exactly once.
Verify lowering capacity never terminates current processes and status consistently identifies every slot holder.
value: Worktree Switcher remains an unobtrusive helper and prevents concurrent agents or projects from exhausting the development machine.
